name: grafito
description: A simple, nice journald web frontend

paragraphs: Grafito is a simple, self-contained web-based log viewer for journalctl. It provides an intuitive interface to browse and filter system logs directly from your web browser.

There is a live demo with fake logs at grafito-demo.ralsina.me. Demo builds are fully interactive: every action button works against the fake world (and the AI explanations are enabled), while nothing ever runs on the demo host.
Context shows the surrounding entries with the inspected one highlighted, and the AI tab holds the explanation.
features: Mission Control UI - a dense, dark ops-dashboard look with a
Inspector side panel - clicking any log entry opens a Detail tab;
Live log tailing over Server-Sent Events (with an automatic fallback
An event frequency chart with adaptive buckets: click a bar to jump
Filtering by unit, tag, hostname, time range, priority and a general

whatItDoes.text: Grafito is a simple, self-contained web-based log viewer for journalctl. It provides an intuitive interface to browse and filter system logs directly from your web browser.

requirements.text: Free ChatJimmy endpoint (hidden behind a flag): Grafito can also talk directly to ChatJimmy's free browser endpoint (Llama 3.1 8B, no API key needed) through its built-in provider — an in-process port of jimmy-proxy, so no sidecar is needed.

The compose view has an Add app button (visible when actions are enabled): a browsable catalog of Runtipi-format app stores, so popular self-hosted tools can be installed as ordinary compose stacks without writing a YAML file.
dot — anything answering below HTTP 500 (redirects and login pages included) counts as up.

The gear button in the top bar opens the settings view (?view=settings): login credentials (with a Sign out button), the display timezone, the AI provider (with API key and model), the homepage basics (title, hostname, weather location), the compose stacks directory, the app store sources and the Gotify notification settings (URL, token, alert thresholds).
